$comment: The honest complement to the interpretation-decision registry: normative requirements the corpus does NOT force, each classified. 'forcible-but-unforced' means a single-statement or multi-statement vector could pin it but none is written yet; 'consumer-policy-unvectorable' means the rule is trust-relative or cross-attestation and cannot be pinned by a self-contained corpus at all. scripts/coverage-matrix-gate.py generates docs/COVERAGE-MATRIX.md from this file plus the registry and fails on drift; the published counts are the measurement the standards play rests on -- 'a corpus can only force what someone thought to write a vector for' becomes a number we drive down rather than a caveat we repeat.

cells.requirement: An out-of-range observationRefs index is a structural fault on ANY row, including an artifact-only row
cells.reason: The rule is basis-independent and implemented on every rail (ref-malformed / ref-out-of-range fire regardless of basis; bad-724 exercises out-of-range on an artifact row, bad-103/108 exercise wrong-type on substrate rows). The one untested cell is the wrong-TYPE variant on an artifact-only row specifically. A single-statement vector could pin it; the rule is already sound, so this is coverage completeness, not a soundness gap.
cells.witnessSketch: bad-7xx-artifact-wrongtype-refs: an artifact-only statement whose observationRefs carries a non-integer or negative index; expected ref-malformed.

cells.requirement: aeeChainScope two-sided equality gate: a consumer admits only the equal declared dimension set, neither a strictly finer (scope-narrowing) nor a strictly coarser (pooling) set
cells.reason: The comparison is consumer policy ACROSS attestations. The conformance corpus is single-statement, so the equality gate cannot be exercised by a self-contained vector; it needs a multi-statement policy vector class (pol-001 narrowed -> reject, pol-002 pooled -> reject, pol-003 exact -> accept), designed in first-party research/163/SEAM-chainscope-narrowing-attack.md and unbuilt.
cells.witnessSketch: A policy/ vector class over statement SETS, not single statements; requires a policy-replay harness the corpus does not currently define.

cells.requirement: Set-vs-tuple reading: policy compares the declared dimension SET; the gap/fork/genesis rules key on the evaluated TUPLE, so genesis-per-subject-value is normal and only a second genesis under an identical tuple is a reset
cells.reason: Same as U2: the distinction only manifests across two or more attestations sharing a substrate key. pol-004 (two-genesis-same-tuple -> equivocation) and pol-005 (two-genesis-different-subject -> NOT equivocation) would pin it in a multi-statement class.
cells.witnessSketch: pol-004 / pol-005 in the unbuilt policy/ class.

cells.requirement: Gap / fork / shared-predecessor / duplicate-genesis detection over a chain
cells.reason: Chain detection is inherently cross-attestation; a single statement carries at most one chain member and cannot exhibit a gap or a fork. Belongs to the policy/ class.
cells.witnessSketch: Multi-statement chains in the policy/ class.

cells.requirement: The anchor comparison (expectedCorpusDigest / expectedSubstrateDigest) and the evidence tier are trust-relative consumer-policy facts, not validity
cells.reason: By design these differ per consumer and are excluded from the byte-pure validity gate; a self-contained corpus vector cannot fix a per-consumer trust anchor. ok-024 exercises the tier under two pinned key policies, which is the most a single-statement vector can do; the anchor comparison itself is out of the corpus's reach by construction.
cells.witnessSketch: None possible in a self-contained corpus; exercised only by a consumer-policy harness.
